watch.en: Cook the flour in the fat over medium heat, stirring often, until it reaches the colour you want.
watch.de: Das Mehl im Fett bei mittlerer Hitze unter häufigem Rühren garen, bis es die gewünschte Farbe hat.

why.en: Cooking the flour in fat softens its flavour and keeps lumps out; a roux that has burnt no longer thickens.
why.de: Das Mehl im Fett zu garen mildert den Mehlgeschmack und hält Klümpchen fern; eine verbrannte Mehlschwitze bindet nicht mehr.

sources.title: Flavors of the Saucier: Stocks, Sauces, and Soups (Zeringue and Thibodeaux)
sources.place: chapter 1.3 Sauces and Thickening Agents, section Procedures for Preparing Roux
sources.sentence: Cook the paste over medium heat until the desired color is achieved. Stir the roux often to avoid burning.

sources.title: Flavors of the Saucier: Stocks, Sauces, and Soups (Zeringue and Thibodeaux)
sources.place: chapter 1.3 Sauces and Thickening Agents, section Roux
sources.sentence: This attenuates the flavor of the flour and eliminates lumps.

sources.title: Flavors of the Saucier: Stocks, Sauces, and Soups (Zeringue and Thibodeaux)
sources.place: chapter 1.3 Sauces and Thickening Agents, section Procedures for Preparing Roux
sources.sentence: Burnt roux will not thicken a liquid; it will simply acid dark specks and an undesirable flavor.
